counterfactual.change: Changed body 1 restitution e from 1 to 0 (single-field change); inelastic second body removes elastic energy gain and no violation occurs.

explanation: Two free circles with e=1 collide (heavy fast body 1 hits light stationary body 0). Energy is conserved (~998 J) through wall bounces until steps 64-65, where a second body-body contact with large mass ratio and high relative speed injects ~133 J, reaching 1131 J above the 1103 J bound. No gravity, walls, or controller work is involved, so the gain must come from the elastic impulse/positional-correction handling over-penetrated fast contacts across substeps.
vision_note: The small upper circle drops vertically onto the larger lower circle, closing the gap through steps 62 to 64 to near-contact. By step 65 the small circle separates slightly upward again, indicating a direct circle-circle collision at the violation time.
